analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to analyze the epidemiological profile of compulsory notifications related to human anti-rabies care in the municipality of Porto Nacional, Tocantins, Brazil, from 2015 to 2025. The research addressed the need for understanding the patterns and characteristics of rabies exposure and management in a specific region to inform public health interventions.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This was an observational, descriptive, retrospective, quantitative, and census-based study using notification data provided by the Municipal Health Surveillance Department. The study covered a period from 2015 to 2025 and included 5,813 records.
analysis.methods: A total of 5,813 records were analyzed, considering sociodemographic variables, characteristics of exposure, prophylactic management, number of recorded vaccine doses, and temporal distribution.
analysis.main_results: The results showed a predominance of males, individuals aged 1 to 19 years, and residents of urban areas. Bites were the main type of exposure, with dogs being the animals most frequently involved. Lower limbs, hands, and feet showed the highest frequencies regarding injury location. The temporal distribution showed fluctuations, with an increase in attendances during the final years of the study period and the highest number of records in 2025.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that these findings may support surveillance, prevention, and health education actions. The study highlighted the importance of understanding the epidemiological profile to tailor interventions effectively.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform surveillance, prevention, and health education actions to reduce the incidence of rabies in the region. Understanding the patterns of exposure and management can help in designing targeted public health interventions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on notification data, which may not capture all cases of rabies exposure. The high frequency of records without registered vaccine doses suggests potential gaps in prophylactic management. The evidence strength is moderate due to the observational nature of the study and the potential for underreporting.

source_body_en: This study aimed to analyze the epidemiological profile of compulsory notifications related to human anti-rabies care in the municipality of Porto Nacional, Tocantins, Brazil, from 2015 to 2025. This was an observational, descriptive, retrospective, quantitative, and censusbased study using notification data provided by the Municipal Health Surveillance Department. A total of 5,813 records were analyzed, considering sociodemographic variables, characteristics of exposure, prophylactic management, number of recorded vaccine doses, and temporal distribution. The results showed a predominance of males, individuals aged 1 to 19 years, and residents of urban areas. Bites were the main type of exposure, with dogs being the animals most frequently involved. Lower limbs, hands, and feet showed the highest frequencies regarding injury location. Animal observation was the most frequently recommended management, and a high frequency of records without registered vaccine doses was observed. The temporal distribution showed fluctuations, with an increase in attendances during the final years of the study period and the highest number of records in 2025. It is concluded that these findings may support surveillance, prevention, and health education actions.

title: Responsible Ownership and Welfare Indicators for Dogs and Cats in Rural Lithuania: Self-Reported Practices and In-Person Assessment
abstract: Dogs and cats are increasingly regarded as companion animals and family members, but companionship requires more than affection: it also entails responsibility for their health, reproduction, housing and behavioural needs. Responsible ownership and welfare in rural Baltic and Eastern European settings remain poorly studied. The study included 383 Lithuanian owners (338 rural, 45 urban) and welfare assessments of 85 animals from 53 rural households using an adapted Animal Welfare Assessment Grid. Animal numbers per household differed significantly by residence (p = 0.0008), with 73.1% of rural respondents keeping two or more animals versus 46.7% of urban respondents. Microchipping of all household animals was less often reported by rural than urban respondents (55.5% vs. 86.7%; p = 0.0003), as was rabies vaccination within the previous three years (67.1% vs. Neutering of all animals was likewise less common in rural households, although not significantly (50.6% vs. Main welfare concerns were environmental enrichment, body condition, frequency of exposure to stressors, behaviour during procedures and the living environment; older animals had poorer scores (p = 0.0004). Rural households kept more animals, while several responsible ownership practices were less consistently implemented, potentially amplifying welfare and population-management consequences and supporting rural education and preventive veterinary initiatives.

abstract_zh: 犬和猫正日益被视为伴侣动物和家庭成员,但陪伴不仅仅需要关爱:它还涉及对其健康、繁殖、居住和行为需求的责任。在农村波罗的海和东欧地区,负责任的饲养和动物福利状况仍缺乏充分研究。本研究纳入了383名立陶宛饲养者(338名农村,45名城市),并使用改良的动物福利评估网格对53个农村家庭中的85只动物进行了福利评估。每户饲养的动物数量在居住地类型上存在显著差异(p = 0.0008),其中73.1%的农村受访者饲养两只或更多动物,而城市受访者中这一比例为46.7%。所有家庭动物的微芯片植入在农村受访者中报告较少(55.5% vs. 86.7%;p = 0.0003),在过去的三年内进行绝育的比例也较低(67.1% vs. 所有动物的绝育在农村家庭中同样较少,但未达到显著差异(50.6% vs. 主要的福利问题包括环境丰富度、身体状况、接触压力源的频率、程序期间的行为以及生活环境;老年动物的评分较差(p = 0.0004)。农村家庭饲养的动物更多,而一些负责任的饲养实践实施得不够一致,这可能加剧动物福利和种群管理方面的后果,并支持农村地区的教育和预防兽医倡议。
